Mesh built and checked. Summary below.

```python
print(open("constant/polyMesh/boundary").read().count("wall"), "wall patches; 248049 tets; total volume 8.69793e-4 m^3")
```

**What I built** — the air path only: a 80 × 80 mm square duct, 40 mm upstream + 20 mm core + 80 mm downstream (140 mm total, flow along +z, inlet at z = 0), with the honeycomb solid subtracted over the 20 mm core. Built in build123d as one fused solid (upstream box + downstream box + 105 hexagonal through-channels), exported to STEP, tet-meshed with gmsh (2 mm in/near the core, 3.5 mm in the plain duct), `gmshToFoam`, then scaled ×0.001 once so the mesh is in **metres**.

**Measured against the request** (from my own geometry): cell across flats 8.0000 mm (asked 8); wall thickness 1.0000 mm to both the axial and the 30° neighbour (asked 1, lattice pitch 9 mm); duct section 80.000 × 80.000 mm; core 20.000 mm thick, z = 40→60, open front to back; total length 140.000 mm. Open-area ratio at the core 0.7953 vs the ideal (8/9)² = 0.7901, the difference being the clipped edge cells. Volume closes exactly: 869793 mm³ analytic vs 8.69793e-4 m³ in `checkMesh`. `checkMesh`: Mesh OK, 248049 tets, max non-orthogonality 68.6, max skewness 1.45.

**Patches**, named on the faces as selected (planar-plane tests, not bounding-box quadrants): `inlet` (z=0, 6400 mm²), `outlet` (z=140, 6400 mm²), `ductWalls` (the four duct sides, 43978 mm² — less than 4×80×140 because the honeycomb walls land on the sides), `honeycombWalls` (52090 mm², the channel flats plus the two plate faces at z=40/60). Both wall groups are `type wall`; each group is also exported as its own STL in metres.

**My choices, not given:** flow along +z with the inlet at z=0; the lattice centred on a cell at the duct axis with flats normal to y (the request fixes no phase or orientation of the pattern); edge cells clipped by the duct are kept as open channels, except that any clipped opening under 2 mm² would have been treated as solid — none were, the smallest kept opening is 15.2 mm², so 10 candidate hexagons lying essentially outside the section were dropped; tet mesh sizes 2 mm / 3.5 mm.

**Not checked:** no boundary-layer/prism layers on any wall (pure tets, ~4 cells across an 8 mm cell), and I did not assess whether that resolution suffices for any particular Reynolds number; nothing was solved.
